title: Zero-shot: SQLAlchemy 1.4 → 2.0 (no recipe; green, 12/13 changes cite verified rules; NVIDIA free tier)

rules.title: Engine-level execute removed; use connection context manager
rules.new_pattern:
with engine.begin() as connection:
    connection.execute(text("INSERT INTO foo (id) VALUES (1)"))
rules.notes: Library-level autocommit removed; explicit `engine.begin()` / `connection.commit()` required; connectionless execution from Engine removed. String statements also require `text()`.

rules.title: engine.connect() legacy; use context manager
rules.notes: `engine.connect()` is legacy; use `with engine.connect()` context manager; implicit autocommit removed. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

rules.title: String SQL requires text() construct
rules.notes: Direct string SQL not supported; must use `text()` function. Applies to `Connection.execute()` and `engine.execute()`. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

rules.title: scalar() requires text() construct
rules.notes: `scalar()` requires `text()` construct; legacy `conn.scalar()` without text removed. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

rules.title: Autocommit removed; explicit transaction required
rules.notes: Implicit autocommit removed; must use explicit transaction control via `engine.begin()` context manager or `conn.commit()`.

rules.title: DML insert/update/delete requires explicit transaction
rules.notes: `insert()` DML no longer auto-commits; requires explicit `engine.begin()` / `commit()`. Same for `update()` and `delete()`.
rules.evidence: insert/update/delete DML no longer accept keyword constructor arguments

rules.title: execute() parameters must be dict or sequence of dicts
rules.notes: Parameters accepted as dict or sequence of dicts only; positional args and `**kwargs` no longer supported. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

rules.title: Result rows act like named tuples
rules.notes: Result rows act like named tuples; column access by index or attribute. `row` access pattern changed.
rules.evidence: Result rows act like named tuples

rules.title: Session.query deprecated; use select()
rules.notes: ORM Query unified with Core Select; `Session.query()` deprecated/removed in favor of `select()`.
rules.evidence: The above bullets refer to the most prominent fully backwards-incompatible changes that are finalized in the 2.0 release. The migration path for applications to accommodate for these changes as well as others is framed as a transition path first into the 1.4 series of SQLAlchemy where the “future” APIs are available to provide for the “2.0” way of working, and then to the 2.0 series where the no-l

rules.title: filter() replaced by where() in core style
rules.notes: `where()` replaces `filter()` in core style; ORM query style unified. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

rules.title: Query.get() moves to Session.get()
rules.notes: `get()` method moves to `Session`; `Query.get()` removed. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

rules.title: join() uses mapped attributes, not strings
rules.notes: Joining/loading on relationships uses attributes, not strings; string attribute names removed. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

rules.title: join(..., aliased=True) and from_joinpoint removed
rules.new_pattern: from sqlalchemy.orm import aliased; order_alias = aliased(Order); select(User).join(User.orders.of_type(order_alias))
rules.notes: `join(..., aliased=True)` and `from_joinpoint` removed; use attribute-based joins with explicit `aliased()`. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

rules.title: lazy='dynamic' relationship deprecated
rules.notes: "Dynamic" relationship loaders superseded by "Write Only" pattern; `lazy='dynamic'` deprecated in favor of `lazy='select'` or `lazy='write'`. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

rules.title: in_()/not_in() explicit subquery syntax changed
rules.notes: `in_()`/`not_in()` accepts column expressions; explicit subquery syntax adjusted.
rules.evidence: Filtering with `in_()`/`not_in()` no longer accepts explicit subqueries

rules.title: DISTINCT with additional columns requires selecting entity
rules.notes: `DISTINCT` with additional columns requires selecting entity alongside columns; old pattern removed. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

rules.title: from_self() pattern changed
rules.notes: `from_self()` pattern changed; selecting from query itself as subquery requires `select().from_self()`. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

rules.title: select_entity_from() replaced by select().select_entity_from()
rules.notes: `Query.select_entity_from()` used for selecting entities from alternative selectables; replaced by `select().select_entity_from()`. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

rules.title: Column-only annotations ignored; Mapped required
rules.notes: `Column`-only annotations ignored by 2.0 Declarative; `Mapped` generic container required for typing.
rules.evidence: Step two - replace Declarative use of `Column` with `mapped_column()`

rules.title: declarative_base() superseded by DeclarativeBase class
rules.old_pattern: from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base; Base = declarative_base()
rules.new_pattern: from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase; class Base(DeclarativeBase): pass
rules.notes: `declarative_base()` function call superseded by using `DeclarativeBase` class directly for typing tool compatibility. [not applied: optional new style; the old usage still works]

rules.title: Column replaced with mapped_column()
rules.notes: `mapped_column()` is the ORM-aware replacement for `Column()` in declarative models; both produce a `Column` internally. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

rules.title: MetaData(bind=engine) removed; pass engine explicitly
rules.notes: `MetaData` no longer auto-binds to `Engine`; explicit engine pass required. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

rules.title: Session(bind=engine) bound metadata removed
rules.notes: Bound metadata removed from `Session`; `Engine` must be passed to `Session` constructor; `bind` parameter deprecated. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

rules.title: sessionmaker(bind=) deprecated
rules.notes: `bind` keyword deprecated in favor of passing `Engine` object directly. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

rules.title: filter_by works but where() preferred
rules.notes: `filter_by` works in core style; `where()` preferred for expression-based filtering; `filter_by` deprecated in favor of `where()` or `Session.get()`. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

rules.title: one() becomes scalar_one() via execute()
rules.notes: `one()` becomes `scalar_one()`; Query interface moves to `select()`/`execute()` pattern. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

rules.title: first() requires scalars() modifier on Result
rules.notes: `first()` requires `scalars()` modifier on Result object; `Query.first()` legacy API. [not applied: optional new style; the old usage still works]

rules.title: count() replaced by Session.scalar(select(func.count()))
rules.notes: `Query.count()` legacy API; new `Session.scalar(select(func.count(...)))` pattern. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

rules.title: isouter parameter handled via outerjoin()
rules.notes: `isouter` parameter handled via `outerjoin()` or `aliased=True` in `join()`. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

rules.title: select() columns positional; whereclause keyword removed
rules.notes: Columns must be passed positionally; `whereclause` keyword argument no longer supported; use `.where()` generative method. [unverified: source page does not support the rule]

Iteration 1: Two main issues: (1) `rename_notebook` passes SQL parameters as separate positional arguments to `execute()`, but SQLAlchemy 2.0 requires a single tuple/dict parameter. (2) `bulk_insert` incorrectly u (2 edits)

Iteration 2: There are two root causes: (1) `rename_notebook` passes parameters as a tuple `(new, old)` to `conn.execute(text(...))`, but SQLAlchemy 2.0 requires a dictionary for named parameters or a list of dict (2 edits)

Iteration 3: The `bulk_insert` test fails because the `notebook_id` column in the `Note` model was implicitly nullable in SQLAlchemy 1.4 (Column defaults to nullable=True), but in SQLAlchemy 2.0 with `Mapped[int]` (1 edits)

Guardrails: 0 violation(s). Ultra review: changes flagged. Migration mostly correct but read-only queries incorrectly use engine.begin() instead of engine.connect(), and get_note() misses identity map optimization.

+# Bumpless characterization harness. Copied verbatim into the target repo as tests/_bumpless/_harness.py.
+# It records what code *does* (data returned, raised vs not raised, exception category), never message text,
+# and serializes values generically so the observation is identical across library versions.
+import builtins
+import dataclasses
+import datetime
+import decimal
+import enum
+import json
+import pathlib
+import sys
+import uuid
+
+ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+if str(ROOT) not in sys.path:
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
+
+_BUILTIN_EXC = tuple(v for v in vars(builtins).values() if isinstance(v, type) and issubclass(v, BaseException))
+
+
+def category(exc: BaseException) -> str:
+    """The first built-in exception class in the MRO (e.g. ValueError), stable across library versions."""
+    for cls in type(exc).__mro__:
+        if cls in _BUILTIN_EXC:
+            return cls.__name__
+    return "Exception"
+
+
+def norm(v, depth=0):
+    if depth > 8:
+        return "<deep>"
+    if v is None or isinstance(v, (bool, int, float)):
+        return v
+    if isinstance(v, str):
+        try:  # JSON text is compared by meaning, not formatting
+            parsed = json.loads(v)
+            if isinstance(parsed, (dict, list)):
+                return {"__json__": norm(parsed, depth + 1)}
+        except ValueError:
+            pass
+        return v
+    if isinstance(v, (datetime.datetime, datetime.date, datetime.time)):
+        return v.isoformat()
+    if isinstance(v, (decimal.Decimal, uuid.UUID, pathlib.PurePath)):
+        return str(v)
+    if isinstance(v, enum.Enum):
+        return norm(v.value, depth + 1)
+    if isinstance(v, bytes):
+        return v.decode("utf-8", "replace")
+    if isinstance(v, dict):
+        return {str(k): norm(x, depth + 1) for k, x in sorted(v.items(), key=lambda kv: str(kv[0]))}
+    if isinstance(v, (list, tuple)):
+        return [norm(x, depth + 1) for x in v]
+    if isinstance(v, (set, frozenset)):
+        return sorted((norm(x, depth + 1) for x in v), key=repr)
+    if dataclasses.is_dataclass(v) and not isinstance(v, type):
+        return {"__type__": type(v).__name__, **norm(dataclasses.asdict(v), depth + 1)}
+    if isinstance(v, type):
+        return {"__class__": v.__name__}
+    if hasattr(v, "__dict__"):
+        public = {k: x for k, x in vars(v).items() if not k.startswith("_")}
+        return {"__type__": type(v).__name__, **norm(public, depth + 1)}
+    return {"__type__": type(v).__name__}
+
+
+OBS: dict = {}
+
+
+def observe(name: str, fn) -> None:
+    try:
+        OBS[name] = {"raised": False, "value": norm(fn())}
+    except Exception as e:  # recording the category is the point
+        OBS[name] = {"raised": True, "category": category(e)}
+
+
+def dump() -> str:
+    return json.dumps(OBS, sort_keys=True, indent=1)
